title: Ford Thunderbird Engines by Year (1955–2005)
description: Every factory engine in the Ford Thunderbird by year: the 292 and supercharged 312, the 352, 390, 428, 429 and 460, the Turbo Coupe and the Super Coupe.
intro: Ford built the Thunderbird from 1955 to 1997 and again from 2002 to 2005, starting as a two-seater and growing into a four-seat personal luxury car. Its engines ran from the Y-block V8s to the 460, and later included the Turbo Coupe's 2.3 turbo four and the Super Coupe's supercharged 3.8.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.
The two-seat Thunderbird used the 292 and 312 Y-block V8s; the 1957 F-code 312 was supercharged.
The four-seat Thunderbird used the 352, the 430 shared with Lincoln in 1959–1960, then the 390, including the 1962–1963 M-code with three two-barrel carburetors, and the 428 for 1966.
The Thunderbird used the 390, 428 and 429 and, from 1972, the 460. Ratings are SAE net from 1972.
The downsized Thunderbird shared Ford's intermediate engines: the 302, 351 and 400.
The Fox and MN12 Thunderbirds offered sixes, the 3.8 V6, the 5.0 and 4.6 V8s, the 1983–1988 Turbo Coupe's 2.3 turbo four, and the 1989–1995 Super Coupe's supercharged 3.8.
The retro Thunderbird used a 3.9 four-cam V8 shared with the Lincoln LS.
